content.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# publish.sh — WordPress Publishing Skill for Scribe (wp-publisher agent)
# =============================================================================
# Usage:
#   bash publish.sh [--title "Title"] [--excerpt "Excerpt"]
#                  [--article /path/to/article.md] [--image /path/to/image.jpg]
#                  [--status publish|draft|pending|future]
#
# Smart extraction: reads SEO Title, Meta Description, URL Slug directly from
# the Writer's META block in the article — no manual passing needed.
#
# Pipeline cleanup: strips META block, Sources footer, Word Count line, and thinking blocks
# before publishing so only clean article content reaches WordPress.
#
# Output (run-scoped — safe for concurrent coinography + memecoinist runs):
#   Exit 0 → $RUN_DIR/publish/wp-url.txt + wordpress.json (canonical)
#            /tmp/${PROJECT_SLUG}-wp-result.txt + .json (per-slug)
#            /tmp/wp-result.txt (legacy best-effort only)
#   Exit 1 → /tmp/wp-error.log contains the human-readable error reason
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# --- Config (project-driven) -------------------------------------------------
# Per-site WordPress credentials + category come from the active project's
# config file, never from hardcoded values. Project resolution order:
#   1. --project flag (if passed)
#   2. $PROJECT_SLUG env
#   3. $PROJECT_CONFIG env (path to projects/<slug>.json)
#   4. $PIPELINE_MANIFEST's "project" field
#   5. fallback: "coinography"
#
# To override the project from the CLI, add `--project <slug>` to the
# argument list (parsed below).

SCRIPT_DIR_PUBLISH="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_CONFIG_PY="$HOME/.openclaw/workspace-orchestrator/skills/pipeline/project_config.py"

POST_STATUS="draft"
PROJECT_ARG=""
CLEAN_MD=""
HTML_PATH=""
ERROR_FILE="/tmp/wp-error.log"
MAX_RETRIES=3

ARTICLE_PATH=""
IMAGE_PATH=""
RUN_DIR=""
RESULT_FILE=""
RESULT_JSON=""
WP_JSON_PATH=""
WP_URL_PATH=""

# --- Helpers (defined early so arg parsing can fatal) ------------------------
log_info()  { echo "[INFO]  $*"; }
log_error() { echo "[ERROR] $*" | tee -a "$ERROR_FILE" >&2; }
fatal()     { log_error "$*"; exit 1; }

# --- Argument Parsing --------------------------------------------------------
TITLE=""
EXCERPT=""

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --title)   TITLE="$2";   shift 2 ;;
    --excerpt) EXCERPT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --article) ARTICLE_PATH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --image)   IMAGE_PATH="$2";   shift 2 ;;
    --project) PROJECT_ARG="$2";  shift 2 ;;
    --status)
      POST_STATUS="$2"
      case "$POST_STATUS" in
        publish|draft|pending|future) ;;
        *) fatal "Invalid --status '$POST_STATUS' (use publish, draft, pending, or future)" ;;
      esac
      shift 2
      ;;
    *) shift ;;
  esac
done

# --- Resolve project -> credentials + paths ----------------------------------
cfg_field() {
  local field="$1"
  if [[ -n "$PROJECT_ARG" ]]; then
    python3 "$PROJECT_CONFIG_PY" --slug "$PROJECT_ARG" --field "$field"
  else
    python3 "$PROJECT_CONFIG_PY" --field "$field"
  fi
}

cfg_password() {
  if [[ -n "$PROJECT_ARG" ]]; then
    python3 "$PROJECT_CONFIG_PY" --slug "$PROJECT_ARG" --password
  else
    python3 "$PROJECT_CONFIG_PY" --password
  fi
}

PROJECT_SLUG_RESOLVED=$(cfg_field slug) || fatal "Cannot resolve project (have you initialized a run?)"
# Reliability gate: resolved project must match the manifest's project.
MANIFEST_PATH="${PIPELINE_MANIFEST:-/tmp/openclaw-active-manifest.json}"
if [[ -f "$MANIFEST_PATH" ]]; then
  MANIFEST_PROJECT=$(python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1])).get('project',''))" "$MANIFEST_PATH" 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [[ -n "$MANIFEST_PROJECT" && "$MANIFEST_PROJECT" != "$PROJECT_SLUG_RESOLVED" ]]; then
    fatal "PROJECT MISMATCH: resolved='$PROJECT_SLUG_RESOLVED' but manifest at $MANIFEST_PATH says project='$MANIFEST_PROJECT'. Aborting to prevent publishing to the wrong site."
  fi
fi
WP_URL=$(cfg_field wordpress.url)             || fatal "missing wordpress.url in project '$PROJECT_SLUG_RESOLVED'"
WP_USER=$(cfg_field wordpress.user)           || fatal "missing wordpress.user in project '$PROJECT_SLUG_RESOLVED'"
WP_PASS=$(cfg_password)                       || fatal "missing wordpress.app_password_ref or password file for '$PROJECT_SLUG_RESOLVED'"
FALLBACK_CATEGORY_ID=$(cfg_field wordpress.fallback_category_id 2>/dev/null || echo "")
# Back-compat: older configs used a single wordpress.category_id.
if [ -z "$FALLBACK_CATEGORY_ID" ]; then
  FALLBACK_CATEGORY_ID=$(cfg_field wordpress.category_id 2>/dev/null || echo "17")
fi
DEFAULT_STATUS=$(cfg_field wordpress.default_status 2>/dev/null || echo "draft")
# If the user didn't pass --status, fall back to the project's default.
if [[ "$POST_STATUS" == "draft" ]] && [[ "$DEFAULT_STATUS" != "draft" ]] && [[ "$DEFAULT_STATUS" != "" ]]; then
  POST_STATUS="$DEFAULT_STATUS"
fi

WP_API="${WP_URL}/wp-json/wp/v2"
RM_API="${WP_URL}/wp-json/rankmath/v1"

# Resolve RUN_DIR from manifest (canonical run bundle root).
if [[ -n "${PIPELINE_MANIFEST:-}" && -f "${PIPELINE_MANIFEST}" ]]; then
  RUN_DIR="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$PIPELINE_MANIFEST" 2>/dev/null || echo "$PIPELINE_MANIFEST")")"
elif [[ -n "${CRYPTO_RUN_DIR:-}" && -d "${CRYPTO_RUN_DIR}" ]]; then
  RUN_DIR="$CRYPTO_RUN_DIR"
fi

# Run-scoped publish outputs (source of truth for build_and_send_card.py).
if [[ -n "$RUN_DIR" ]]; then
  mkdir -p "${RUN_DIR}/publish"
  WP_JSON_PATH="${RUN_DIR}/publish/wordpress.json"
  WP_URL_PATH="${RUN_DIR}/publish/wp-url.txt"
fi

# Per-slug /tmp paths (safe across concurrent runs; legacy /tmp/crypto-* still
# resolve via init_run.sh symlinks for coinography backward compat).
RESULT_FILE="/tmp/${PROJECT_SLUG_RESOLVED}-wp-result.txt"
RESULT_JSON="/tmp/${PROJECT_SLUG_RESOLVED}-wp-result.json"
ARTICLE_PATH="${ARTICLE_PATH:-/tmp/${PROJECT_SLUG_RESOLVED}-article.md}"
if [[ -z "${IMAGE_PATH:-}" ]]; then
  if [[ -n "$RUN_DIR" && -f "${RUN_DIR}/media/feature.jpg" ]]; then
    IMAGE_PATH="${RUN_DIR}/media/feature.jpg"
  else

import sys
import re
import random
import hashlib
import time
import requests
from urllib.parse import urlparse, urljoin, quote

def solve_pow(challenge_str, complexity):
    challenge_bytes = challenge_str.encode('utf-8')
    c = random.randint(0, 5000000)
    
    # We need the first 'complexity' bits of SHA-1(challenge + c_bytes) to be zero.
    # In Python, we can check this by examining the top bits of the first 4 bytes of SHA1.
    shift = 32 - complexity
    
    print(f"Solving PoW for challenge: '{challenge_str}' with complexity: {complexity}...", file=sys.stderr)
    start_time = time.time()
    hashes = 0
    
    while True:
        # Minimal big-endian representation of c
        if c <= 255:
            c_bytes = bytes([c])
        elif c <= 65535:
            c_bytes = bytes([c >> 8, c & 255])
        elif c <= 16777215:
            c_bytes = bytes([c >> 16, (c >> 8) & 255, c & 255])
        else:
            c_bytes = bytes([c >> 24, (c >> 16) & 255, (c >> 8) & 255, c & 255])
            
        data = challenge_bytes + c_bytes
        h = hashlib.sha1(data).digest()
        
        # Get the first 32-bit word in big-endian
        first_word = int.from_bytes(h[:4], 'big')
        
        # Check leading bits
        if (first_word >> shift) == 0:
            elapsed = int((time.time() - start_time) * 1000)
            print(f"Solution found: c={c}, hashes={hashes}, elapsed={elapsed}ms", file=sys.stderr)
            return c, elapsed, hashes
            
        c += 1
        hashes += 1

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print("Usage: python3 sg_solver.py <target_url>", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
        
    url = sys.argv[1]
    
    # Start requests session to persist cookies
    session = requests.Session()
    session.headers.update({
        'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36'
    })
    
    # Step 1: Request target URL to trigger challenge page
    print(f"Requesting target: {url} ...", file=sys.stderr)
    r = session.get(url, timeout=30)
    
    if r.status_code == 200 and 'sgchallenge' not in r.text:
        print("No challenge found! Already accessible.", file=sys.stderr)
        # Save cookies anyway
        save_cookies(session, "wp_cookies.txt")
        return
        
    # Step 2: Parse challenge page
    html = r.text
    challenge_match = re.search(r'const\s+sgchallenge\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', html)
    submit_url_match = re.search(r'const\s+sgsubmit_url\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', html)
    
    if not challenge_match or not submit_url_match:
        print("Failed to find sgchallenge or sgsubmit_url in HTML response!", file=sys.stderr)
        print("Response body snippet:", html[:1000], file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
        
    sgchallenge = challenge_match.group(1)
    sgsubmit_url = submit_url_match.group(1)
    
    complexity = int(sgchallenge.split(':', 1)[0])
    
    # Step 3: Solve PoW
    sol, elapsed, hashes = solve_pow(sgchallenge, complexity)
    
    # Step 4: Submit solution
    # The submission url format from JS:
    # i + (i.indexOf("?") > -1 ? "&" : "?") + "sol=" + encodeURIComponent(t) + "&s=" + String(e) + ":" + String(r)
    # Note: t is the solution sol, e is the elapsed time, r is the number of hashes.
    parsed_submit = urlparse(sgsubmit_url)
    submit_path = parsed_submit.path
    submit_query = parsed_submit.query
    
    sol_url = urljoin(url, sgsubmit_url)
    sep = '&' if '?' in sol_url else '?'
    sol_url += f"{sep}sol={quote(str(sol))}&s={elapsed}:{hashes}"
    
    print(f"Submitting solution to: {sol_url} ...", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Make GET request to solution URL
    # Important: SiteGround might redirect us, let's follow redirects
    sol_r = session.get(sol_url, allow_redirects=True, timeout=30)
    
    print(f"Solution response status: {sol_r.status_code}", file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Check cookies
    print("Cookies after solving:", session.cookies.get_dict(), file=sys.stderr)
    
    # Step 5: Save cookies
    save_cookies(session, "wp_cookies.txt")
    print("SUCCESS: Session cookies saved to wp_cookies.txt", file=sys.stderr)

def save_cookies(session, filepath):
    with open(filepath, 'w') as f:
        # Save in Curl cookie jar format
        f.write("# Netscape HTTP Cookie File\n")
        for cookie in session.cookies:
            domain = cookie.domain
            # prefix with dot if domain matches subdomains but not host exactly (Netscape standard)
            initial_dot = "TRUE" if domain.startswith('.') else "FALSE"
            path = cookie.path
            secure = "TRUE" if cookie.secure else "FALSE"
            expires = str(cookie.expires) if cookie.expires else "0"
            name = cookie.name
            value = cookie.value
            f.write(f"{domain}\t{initial_dot}\t{path}\t{secure}\t{expires}\t{name}\t{value}\n")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import sys
import re
import random
import hashlib
import time
import requests
import base64
from urllib.parse import urlparse, urljoin, quote

def solve_pow(challenge_str, complexity):
    challenge_bytes = challenge_str.encode('utf-8')
    c = random.randint(0, 5000000)
    
    shift = 32 - complexity
    
    print(f"Solving PoW for challenge: '{challenge_str}' with complexity: {complexity}...", file=sys.stderr)
    start_time = time.time()
    hashes = 0
    
    while True:
        if c <= 255:
            c_bytes = bytes([c])
        elif c <= 65535:
            c_bytes = bytes([c >> 8, c & 255])
        elif c <= 16777215:
            c_bytes = bytes([c >> 16, (c >> 8) & 255, c & 255])
        else:
            c_bytes = bytes([c >> 24, (c >> 16) & 255, (c >> 8) & 255, c & 255])
            
        data = challenge_bytes + c_bytes
        h = hashlib.sha1(data).digest()
        
        first_word = int.from_bytes(h[:4], 'big')
        
        if (first_word >> shift) == 0:
            elapsed = int((time.time() - start_time) * 1000)
            # The JS code returns o().stringify(f) which is base64 of the challenge_bytes + c_bytes.
            # But wait, does it pad or clamp?
            # Let's use standard base64 encoding of data.
            solution_b64 = base64.b64encode(data).decode('utf-8')
            print(f"Solution found: c={c}, hashes={hashes}, elapsed={elapsed}ms", file=sys.stderr)
            print(f"Solution Base64: {solution_b64}", file=sys.stderr)
            return solution_b64, elapsed, hashes
            
        c += 1
        hashes += 1

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print("Usage: python3 sg_solver.py <target_url>", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
        
    url = sys.argv[1]
    
    session = requests.Session()
    session.headers.update({
        'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36'
    })
    
    print(f"Requesting target: {url} ...", file=sys.stderr)
    r = session.get(url, timeout=30)
    
    refresh_match = re.search(r'content="0;url=([^"]+)"', r.text, re.IGNORECASE)
    if not refresh_match:
        refresh_match = re.search(r"content='0;url=([^']+)'", r.text, re.IGNORECASE)
    if not refresh_match:
        refresh_match = re.search(r'content="0;\s*([^"]+)"', r.text, re.IGNORECASE)
        
    if refresh_match:
        redirect_url = urljoin(url, refresh_match.group(1).replace('&', '&'))
        print(f"Meta refresh redirect detected: {redirect_url} ...", file=sys.stderr)
        r = session.get(redirect_url, timeout=30)
        
    html = r.text
    if r.status_code == 200 and 'sgchallenge' not in html:
        print("No challenge found! Already accessible.", file=sys.stderr)
        save_cookies(session, "wp_cookies.txt")
        return
        
    challenge_match = re.search(r'const\s+sgchallenge\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', html)
    submit_url_match = re.search(r'const\s+sgsubmit_url\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', html)
    
    if not challenge_match or not submit_url_match:
        print("Failed to find sgchallenge or sgsubmit_url in HTML response!", file=sys.stderr)
        print("Response body snippet:", html[:1000], file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
        
    sgchallenge = challenge_match.group(1)
    sgsubmit_url = submit_url_match.group(1)
    
    complexity = int(sgchallenge.split(':', 1)[0])
    
    sol_b64, elapsed, hashes = solve_pow(sgchallenge, complexity)
    
    sol_url = urljoin(url, sgsubmit_url)
    sep = '&' if '?' in sol_url else '?'
    sol_url += f"{sep}sol={quote(sol_b64)}&s={elapsed}:{hashes}"
    
    print(f"Submitting solution to: {sol_url} ...", file=sys.stderr)
    
    session.headers.update({
        'Referer': r.url
    })
    
    sol_r = session.get(sol_url, allow_redirects=True, timeout=30)
    
    print(f"Solution response status: {sol_r.status_code}", file=sys.stderr)
    print(f"Solution response headers:\n{sol_r.headers}", file=sys.stderr)
    print("Cookies after solving:", session.cookies.get_dict(), file=sys.stderr)
    
    with open('/tmp/sol_r.html', 'w') as f:
        f.write(sol_r.text)
        
    save_cookies(session, "/tmp/wp_cookies.txt")
    print("SUCCESS: Session cookies saved to /tmp/wp_cookies.txt", file=sys.stderr)

def save_cookies(session, filepath):
    with open(filepath, 'w') as f:
        f.write("# Netscape HTTP Cookie File\n")
        for cookie in session.cookies:
            domain = cookie.domain
            initial_dot = "TRUE" if domain.startswith('.') else "FALSE"
            path = cookie.path
            secure = "TRUE" if cookie.secure else "FALSE"
            expires = str(cookie.expires) if cookie.expires else "0"
            name = cookie.name
            value = cookie.value
            f.write(f"{domain}\t{initial_dot}\t{path}\t{secure}\t{expires}\t{name}\t{value}\n")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
